_comment: Example task project registry. Copy to $COFFERDAM_HOME/config/task-projects.json
and edit on the workstation — this file is an example and is never read by the
service.
A project says WHERE a task may run. It never says what to run: there is no
field for a command, argv, an environment, a shell string or a script, and an
entry carrying one is refused by name rather than ignored.
'root' must be a plain absolute path — no ~, no $VAR, no '..'. It is verified
again immediately before every task starts: each component is checked for a
symlink, the resolved path must equal the configured one, and it must be a
readable directory. A root reached through a link is refused.
'adapters' is an allowlist, and an empty list means NONE rather than all — so a
future adapter never silently gains access to an existing project. Names this
build does not know are dropped rather than failing the entry.
'delegated_adapter' says WHICH of those actually runs when the caller did not
name one — which is every task started through the Actions bridge, because
createTask has no adapter field. Omit it when 'adapters' has exactly one entry:
there is nothing to choose between and Cofferdam resolves it. Set it as soon as
there are two, because a project permitting several and delegating to none is
refused rather than guessed at. It must name an adapter the same entry permits
and this build registered; anything else also refuses.
Nothing is auto-registered. A registry that scanned your home directory and
offered what it found would grant access by accident.
See docs/AGENT_TASK_CORE.md.

projects.display_name: A project that permits both Claude transports
projects.notes: delete the delegated_adapter line and no task can start here
